report:
NO DEFECTS

I found no defect at head `12927ccd` that I can show. The time budget ended before I had read all ~17.5k diff lines. I did not have the prior head (`a0b32f7a`) on disk, so I couldn't diff round to round. Instead I checked each earlier finding against the current source, reran the PR's own focused tests, and ran one probe of my own (Bun WebSocket async context). I did **not** replay the earlier rounds' endpoint probes (`hold-retry`, `wire-admission`, `raw-gap`, `annotation-attacks`) here. A finding below marked "closed" means closed in the source and covered by the PR's tests, not re-measured.

## NOT A DEFECT

**Status of each earlier finding at this head**

| Earlier finding | Status | What I saw at this head |
|---|---|---|
| claude F1: a retry parked in the provider's backoff is sent after the hold engages | Closed (source) | `request-hold.ts:118-138` `installFetchHold` wraps `globalThis.fetch` for the whole process. Any fetch made in a held scope goes to `refuseHeld` instead of the real fetch, so each retry is checked at the moment it is sent. `stream.ts` `withRequestHold` now checks only on entry and relies on the fetch wrapper and the WebSocket checks for every later attempt. |
| claude F2 / astra raw-adapter P1: Perplexity's direct `streamOpenAI*` calls, Hindsight, MCP, Exa and `withOAuthAccess` bypass the hold | Closed (source) | All of these go through `fetch`. `openai-responses.ts:826` looks up `options?.fetch ?? fetch` on each call, so it gets the wrapper. `perplexity.ts:511-526` now carries `model-request: turn`. `runOAuthAttempt` checks the hold before each attempt (`auth-retry.ts`). |
| claude F3: checker accepts a signal deleted behind a helper | Closed (checker) | The header of `model-request-ownership.ts` (lines 49-52) says options built by a helper are accepted only when the helper's arguments visibly carry the signal. The checker test passes: 32/32 together with the selftest file. It reports 384 sites in 12 packages. |
| claude F4 / astra checker P2: `globalThis["fetch"]`, destructured fetch, later-spread and conditional undefined signals | Mostly closed | The checker now handles computed and destructured globals, spreads ("a later spread wins") and conditionals ("every branch must carry one"). I did not re-run the computed-specifier or outside-`src` attacks. |
| claude F5: a tool call already in flight is not held | Closed | A tool's own fetch now goes through the global fetch wrapper. |
| claude "late survivor leak" | Addressed | `bindOwnerDisposal`'s unbind, and a rebind over an owner whose disposal already fired, both run `#cancelHeldJobs` (`job-manager.ts:769-799`). |
| astra P1: microtask gap between admission and send | Closed (source) | `withAuth` and `runOAuthAttempt` use `if (isRequestHeld()) await admit…` followed by the attempt in the same turn. The fetch wrapper checks in the same call that sends. |
| astra P1: a job that begins its owner's disposal during startup is never found | Closed (source) | `#jobs.set(id, job)` and `#stopForDisposingOwner(job)` now run before the body starts (`job-manager.ts:469-477`). |
| astra P1: `/security cloud start` sends after full disposal | Closed (source) | `security.ts:275-342` passes `cloudCommandSignal` (session dispose signal joined with the runtime signal) to every cloud call. New test file: `test/security/cloud-command-disposal.test.ts`. |
| astra P1: live-call signaling sent after the controller stopped | Closed (source) | `live/transport.ts:195-260` adds `#throwIfEnded()` after each await and passes `signal` to `withOAuthAccess` and to the fetch. |
| astra P2: a nested hold keeps a request waiting after the owner ends | Closed (source) | `refuseHeld` (`request-hold.ts:73-85`) collects the `ended` signal of every enclosing scope. `isHeld` walks up the parent chain. |

**Suspicions I ruled out**

- **WebSocket callbacks might lose the hold scope.** If they did, the per-frame checks in GitLab Duo (`send`) and Codex would pass silently. Probe `als-ws.test.ts` against a real `Bun.serve` WebSocket printed `{"onopen":"scope","onmessage":"scope","listener":"scope"}`. Bun keeps the scope in `onopen`, `onmessage` and `addEventListener`, so the checks do fire.
- **Fetch wrapper metadata.** It copies the wrapped function's own properties (e.g. `fetch.preconnect`) and skips `length`, `name` and `prototype`. It installs itself only once per fetch it wraps, and wrapping a test spy again is harmless.
- **`AgentLifecycleManager.dispose` loop.** `while (#teardownReleases.size > 0) await Promise.all(...)` cannot spin forever. Each `settled.then(delete)` is attached before `Promise.all` subscribes, so the entry is removed before the loop checks again. Each release is also bounded by the teardown deadline through `untilAborted`.
- **Subagent memory flushes refused inside a held scope.** Mnemopi subagent state is an alias of the parent's (`backend.ts:125-137`), so durable flushes run in the parent's context, outside the hold.
- **Shared work stalled by one held caller.** Token refresh, usage, resets, AWS/Google credentials, catalog discovery and the antigravity version fetch all start inside `runOutsideRequestHold`.
